briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 2, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Failure to Meet Policy Targets
sections.content: Global greenhouse gas concentrations have reached record highs, with scientists warning that even a temporary overshoot of 1.5℃ could lead to irreversible glacier loss [8, 10, 95]. Amidst the spread of global extreme weather events, such as Bolivia declaring a national emergency due to the Super El Niño phenomenon [11, 93], domestic climate policies, despite being expanded across the entire economy, are still falling short of achieving their targets [2, 21]. This, coupled with the perception that climate change threatens the American Dream [94, 99], is also leading to pessimistic outlooks that the Paris Agreement alone cannot avert the crisis [106]. In particular, climate-vulnerable African nations are facing a situation where millions are exposed to extreme climate risks due to gaps in early warning systems [111], and even the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) does not consider climate change a major financial risk [120], indicating an overall inadequacy in response efforts.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutral Lifestyle Practices and Efforts to Expand Renewable Energy
sections.content: Various domestic efforts to respond to the climate crisis are underway. Along with an analysis suggesting that the cost of achieving carbon neutrality is less than the price of neglecting the climate crisis [4], several local governments, including Siheung City, have been re-designated as environmental education cities, expanding carbon neutrality practices [14, 29, 36, 37, 54, 57]. Gyeongsan City supports participation in carbon neutrality points for apartment complexes [16, 52, 60], and resident-participatory carbon-neutral lifestyle practice campaigns have been successfully held in numerous areas, including Yeoncheon County and Suwon City [15, 26, 31, 32, 35, 40, 42, 55, 56, 58, 64]. Furthermore, efforts to accelerate the transition to eco-friendly mobility are gaining momentum, with nationwide signature campaigns for electric vehicle adoption and policies offering carbon points for purchase commitments being implemented [38, 43, 44, 49, 53, 62, 65, 45, 48, 51, 63]. In the corporate and public sectors, Hyundai Steel's completion of solar power generation [18], Korea District Heating Corporation's carbon neutrality and AI-centric management strategy restructuring [27, 34], and Seoul City's policy to expand renewable energy installations in buildings [69] highlight significant transition efforts. Additionally, the surge in China's clean technology exports demonstrates its potential to contribute to global carbon emission reductions [6, 76, 78].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Challenges in Expanding Renewable Energy and Policy Discussions
sections.content: Despite positive movements in renewable energy transition, several challenges are emerging. The provincial council has put a brake on Jeonbuk Development Corporation's expansion of its renewable energy organization [67], and Saemangeum Development Corporation's re-bidding for RE100 and Smart Green Industrial Complex renewable energy operators, which is being repeated due to a single bidder [68, 70, 77, 80, 82, 85, 86], illustrates the difficulties in project implementation. In particular, in the Jeju region, electricity tariffs and grid improvements are being pointed out as obstacles to renewable energy expansion [71, 74], and an unreasonable case has emerged where corporate bond interest in offshore wind projects is being covered by residents' shares, raising questions about exemplary models for citizen participation [89]. Furthermore, concerns are being raised about the potential impact of strengthening the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act on agricultural and marine ecosystems [9], leading to growing calls for enhanced citizen participation and expanded economic compensation in the energy sector [20, 22, 61].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Action and the Need for Adaptation
sections.content: Globally, awareness of climate change impacts and adaptation efforts are being pursued from various angles. Amidst active research, including California's release of its climate change assessment report [101] and Spelman College's NASA-supported research [115], expectations and concerns from various nations are converging ahead of the COP31 Climate Summit, with predictions that it could be the most disappointing summit to date [98, 103, 104, 125]. Insurance companies are facing climate change risks related to new AI data centers [105], and anxiety about climate change is affecting students [102], indicating a broadening impact across society. Meanwhile, IPCC authors have met in Tanzania to advance climate change reports [117], and in India, a classroom initiative linking menstrual health and climate change has won an international award [121], demonstrating ongoing diverse attempts and international cooperation for climate change adaptation [109].

briefing.closing: Today's news once again reminds us of the severity of the climate crisis and the urgent need for global and local response efforts. This concludes today's climate briefing.
